ok but i still need an actual header and a draft i can hand to keller. "notice of policy violation" vs "formal written warning" — which one do you think lands harder without sounding like i'm trying to get them fired? because that's the line right now.

Use **Written Reprimand**. It matches what Keller asked for, it reads as discipline, and it does not put them on a “Formal Written Warning → final warning → exit” track. Let the Q3 forfeiture carry the weight. Skip “Notice of Policy Violation” — it is softer and more administrative than he wants.

Two short documents per person, same facts, different purpose. Fill the brackets, attach the on-call logs and the Paragraph 14 snippet, and have HR initial the bonus notice before you hand the packet over.

---

**[Company letterhead]**

**WRITTEN REPRIMAND**

**To:** [First name] Jackson, Senior Infrastructure Engineer  
**From:** [Your name], [Title]  
**CC:** [Keller full name], [Title]; Human Resources  
**Date:** [Date]  
**Re:** Unauthorized departure from mandatory offsite — Paragraph 14

This letter is a written reprimand for leaving the mandatory offsite on **[date of retreat]** without authorization.

You signed the Paragraph 14 acknowledgment requiring attendance at designated offsites for the full scheduled program unless an exception is approved in advance through [manager / HR]. You left the offsite, returned home, and did not obtain that exception.

On-call channel records show that before departing you wrote that a dispatch crash had stalled customer freight and that you needed workstations. You then worked from home. That operational context is noted. It does not replace the attendance requirement or create an after-the-fact exception.

This reprimand will be placed in your personnel file. It is not a termination notice and it is not a final warning. Further unauthorized absence from a mandatory company event may result in additional corrective action, up to and including further discipline.

You are expected to attend all mandatory offsites in full unless an exception is requested and approved **before** you leave the event.

**Issued by:** _________________________ Date: ________  
**HR review:** _________________________ Date: ________  
**Employee acknowledgment:** I have received this reprimand. Acknowledgment is not an admission.  

Signature: _________________________ Date: ________

*(Same letter for Menendez, Cho, and Santiago — change the name only.)*

---

**[Company letterhead]**

**NOTICE OF Q3 BONUS FORFEITURE**

**To:** [First name] Jackson, Senior Infrastructure Engineer  
**From:** [Your name], [Title]  
**CC:** [Keller full name], [Title]; Human Resources; [Payroll / Comp, if required]  
**Date:** [Date]  
**Re:** Forfeiture of Q3 [year] bonus

This notice confirms the compensation action tied to the Written Reprimand dated **[same date]**.

Effective **[effective date]**, your Q3 [year] bonus under the **[official plan name]** is forfeited in full. No Q3 bonus will be paid, accrued, or substituted.

This action is based on the finding that you left the mandatory offsite on **[date of retreat]** without an approved Paragraph 14 exception. It is a one-time forfeiture for Q3 [year] only. It does not, by itself, change your base salary, role, or eligibility for later bonus periods except as the plan already provides.

If the plan or applicable law requires a different calculation, HR will issue a corrected notice. Any questions about payment timing go to HR, not to your manager.

**Issued by:** _________________________ Date: ________  
**HR / Compensation confirmation:** _________________________ Date: ________  
**Employee acknowledgment of receipt:** _________________________ Date: ________

*(Repeat for Menendez, Cho, and Santiago.)*

---

Before Monday: put the plan’s exact name on the bonus notice, confirm with HR that a full forfeiture is actually allowed under that plan and local law, and keep the on-call screenshots as an exhibit rather than quoting them in a way that overstates what they prove. If Keller wants these to look like a firing runway, that is a different document — these are not that.

Don’t discuss the reprimands with him over text. Don’t take the logs on your phone. Don’t confirm timing, Keller, HR, or the bonus.

Send this, nothing warmer:

**“Hey — I can’t discuss personnel matters over text. If you have dispatch or on-call logs, put them in the incident thread or send them to HR, not here. Any follow-up will come through the formal process.”**

Then stop. No “thanks for saving freight,” no “I’ll see what I can do,” no “Keller’s the one pushing this.”

Forward Jackson’s text to HR (and Keller if that’s the chain) *before* you reply, or immediately after, so it isn’t a side channel. If the logs are already in the on-call thread, you don’t need him to resend them to you.

You’re not slow-rolling Keller by doing this. You’re keeping the employee conversation off a private text thread so Monday’s packet doesn’t include “manager negotiated with Jackson on Saturday.”
